examples.text: 职场是一个火锅，想想真的够吓人的。
examples.trans: The workplace is a hotpot; just thinking about it is scary enough.

examples.text: 职场是一个火锅，想想真的够吓人的。
examples.trans: The workplace is a hotpot; just thinking about it is scary enough.

examples.text: 最后留下的概率并不是很高。
examples.trans: The chance of staying on at the end is really not very high.

examples.text: 不要太着急了，招聘竞争都很激烈。
examples.trans: Do not get too anxious; the hiring competition is very fierce.

二位.gloss: the two of you, both of you

meanings.en: the two of you, both of you

examples.text: 二位真是说得比唱得好听。
examples.trans: The two of you truly talk sweeter than a song.

examples.text: 请问二位今天想喝点什么茶？
examples.trans: What tea would the two of you like today?

examples.text: 他的习惯是不带实习生的。
examples.trans: His habit is never taking on interns.

examples.text: 有些人的名字不能提，你提到他，他就会出现。
examples.trans: Some people's names must not be mentioned; if you mention him, he will appear.

examples.text: 你们俩要做好思想准备。
examples.trans: The two of you need to be mentally prepared.

examples.text: 学校几个球友打不过我，嫌没劲。
examples.trans: None of the campus players could beat me, so they complained it wasn't fun.

examples.text: 这几天又有几个八卦微博在说你已婚的事情，我们经纪部出了几个方案，需要你配合一下。
examples.trans: Over the past few days several gossip accounts on Weibo started claiming you're secretly married; management drafted response plans for you.

examples.text: 你是联合制作人的助理，跟我们不一样。
examples.trans: You are the co-producer's assistant — you are different from us.

examples.text: 你最期待哪位明星在红毯亮相？
examples.trans: Which star do you most look forward to seeing?

examples.text: 请问刚才是哪位打来的电话？
examples.trans: May I ask who called on the phone just now?

examples.text: 我想问一下，方教授在哪办公啊？
examples.trans: May I ask where Professor Fang has his office?

examples.text: 谈到义务了，你跟洛琳的过去到底是怎么一回事？
examples.trans: Speaking of duty, then — what exactly happened in the past between you and Luo Lin?

examples.text: 这件事我们再商量一下。
examples.trans: Let's discuss this matter a bit more.

examples.text: 职场是一个火锅，想想真的够吓人的。
examples.trans: The workplace is a hotpot; just thinking about it is scary enough.

examples.text: 你以前不是说女人最可怕吗？
examples.trans: Did you not say before that women are the scariest?

examples.text: 她是一位独立又自信的职场女人。
examples.trans: She is an independent, confident career woman.

examples.text: 我觉得还是让她来讲解一下比较好。
examples.trans: I think it would be better to have her explain it.

examples.text: 我觉得还是让她来讲解一下比较好。
examples.trans: I think it would be better to have her explain it.

examples.text: 感觉非常好，还要谢谢方老师推荐。
examples.trans: It feels great, and I also want to thank Professor Fang for the recommendation.

examples.text: 你早晚会成长的，要对自己有信心。
examples.trans: Sooner or later you will grow; you need to have confidence in yourself.

examples.text: 不要太着急了，招聘竞争都很激烈。
examples.trans: Do not get too anxious; the hiring competition is very fierce.

examples.text: 那儿就是淳于乔的总编室。
examples.trans: Over there is Chun Yuqiao's chief editor's office.

examples.text: 在那边，要不我带您过去？
examples.trans: Over there — how about I take you over?

meanings.note: Visible surprise at unexpected news or visitors.

examples.text: 看到新上任的主管竟然是他，大家都十分惊讶。
examples.trans: Seeing that the new chief was him left everyone thoroughly astonished.

examples.text: 她冷静老练的表现让在场的高管们感到惊讶。
examples.trans: Her poised, seasoned presentation surprised the executives in the room.

meanings.note: Reduplicated suffix in 亮晶晶 or 粉晶晶.

examples.text: 舞台灯光照在她粉晶晶的礼服上格外好看。
examples.trans: Stage lights gleamed prettily across her glittery pink dress.

examples.text: 小姑娘眨着一双亮晶晶的眼睛认真听讲。
examples.trans: The young girl listened intently with bright, sparkling eyes.
May I ask what is your business?
What is your business looking for me?

examples.text: 星天也在用我们提供的数据。
examples.trans: Xingtian is also using the data we provide.

examples.text: 我看他们太忙了，就想上去帮把手。
examples.trans: I saw they were too busy, so I wanted to step up and lend a hand.

meanings.note: Evaluative verb phrase judging by outward appearance.

examples.text: 他和老朋友一边喝茶一边聊天，神情看起来非常轻松。
examples.trans: Chatting over tea with an old friend, he looked thoroughly relaxed.

examples.text: 这份策划案表面上看起来简单，执行起来却很有难度。
examples.trans: This proposal looks simple on paper yet takes real skill to execute.

examples.text: 不要老想着自己是实习生没经验。
examples.trans: Stop always thinking that you are an intern with no experience.

meanings.note: Short color adjective modifying clothes or decor.

examples.text: 为了迎接好消息，她特意穿了一件亮眼的粉外套上班。
examples.trans: Expecting good news, she wore a bright pink jacket to work.

examples.text: 春天来了，公园里的樱花开得粉嫩迷人。
examples.trans: Spring arrived, and cherry blossoms bloomed soft pink across the park.

examples.text: 全公司的人都知道了，昨天他接你下班，今天又来送你上班，你的衣服也没有换。
examples.trans: The whole company knows! He picked you up yesterday, drove you in today, and you haven't even changed clothes.

examples.text: 这件事我们再商量一下。
examples.trans: Let's discuss this matter a bit more.

examples.text: 你敢说你不是为了他，放弃到手的金饭碗？

迎接.gloss: welcome, greet on arrival, meet (a challenge)

meanings.en: welcome, greet on arrival, meet (a challenge)
meanings.note: Greeting returning people or new milestones.

examples.text: 她特意换上喜庆的衣服，满心欢喜地准备迎接老搭档回归。
examples.trans: She dressed up brightly, eager to welcome her old boss back.

examples.text: 整个制作中心严阵以待，准备迎接周末晚间的大直播考验。
examples.trans: The whole center stood ready to meet the weekend live-broadcast test.

examples.text: 不要太着急了，招聘竞争都很激烈。
examples.trans: Do not get too anxious; the hiring competition is very fierce.

examples.text: 灯光下她外套上的亮片一闪一闪的，显得格外活泼精神。
examples.trans: Sequins on her jacket twinkled in the light, looking lively and bright.

examples.text: 导播台上的红色提示灯一闪，提醒主持人直播正式开始。
examples.trans: The red tally light flashed on the console, cueing the host live.

examples.text: 感觉非常好，还要谢谢方老师推荐。
